name: Virginia OAA — locality grants (FY27 final new-award window 10/27 / FY28 apps due 3/2/2027)
funder: VA Opioid Abatement Authority
heart: Every VA city and county has a settlement allocation it can only unlock by getting an abatement project approved. Get MORE named as the evidence-based training contractor in locality applications before the 10/27/2026 final new-FY2027 cutoff, or in FY2028 new applications (due 3/2/2027).
portal: OAA Grants Portal (voaagrants.us) — held by the locality; MORE enters via the locality's contractor budget
accounts_needed: Virginia eVA (free)

name: OJJDP FY 2026 Juvenile Drug Treatment Court Program
funder: U.S. DOJ, Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention (OJJDP)
program: Juvenile Drug Treatment Court Program (Cat 1 Planning & Implementation; Cat 2 Enhancement)
heart: Funds governments to start (Cat 1) or enhance (Cat 2) juvenile drug treatment courts for youth with SUD or co-occurring MH and substance use disorders. Cat 2 explicitly covers improving 'the quality and types of treatment services', so MORE training for the JDTC's treatment provider could be a contractual line item. MORE's fit is weakened because the program is youth-only and very small (4 awards).
accounts_needed: SAM.gov (UEI), Grants.gov, JustGrants: all held by the government applicant
match_required: Yes: 25% of total project costs (cash and/or in-kind); applications without match are ineligible
page_limit: Proposal Questionnaire answers 1-2 paragraphs each; abstract max 2,000 characters
attachments: SF-424; Proposal Questionnaire; Budget Detail Worksheet; Letters of Commitment (Cat 1 required: judge, prosecutor, defense, treatment provider, coordinator, law enforcement, community supervision); Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (if applicable); Consultant Rate (if applicable); Tribal Authorizing Resolution (if applicable); Financial Management and System of Internal Controls Questionnaire
scoring_map: Description of the Need 5%; Project Goals and Objectives 15%; Project Design and Implementation 35% (name subrecipients if known); Capabilities and Competencies 30%; Budget 15%

name: BJA Adult Treatment Court Program (FY26)
funder: U.S. DOJ — Bureau of Justice Assistance
heart: About $49M for courts and counties to plan, run, or expand adult treatment courts. Clinical training for court treatment providers is a natural budget line, so MORE gets in through a county or court applicant.
accounts_needed: partner's SAM/Grants.gov/JustGrants

name: BJA COSSUP Training & Technical Assistance (FY26)
funder: U.S. DOJ — Bureau of Justice Assistance
heart: One national award to train and advise COSSUP grantees on overdose and substance-use responses in the justice system, and for-profits may apply. MORE fits best as the clinical-training partner inside a national TTA provider's bid.
accounts_needed: SAM/UEI, Grants.gov, JustGrants
scoring_map: TTA in four core areas starting with pre-booking operations; position MORE as the treatment-side curriculum.

name: OJJDP FY 2026 Opioid Affected Youth Initiative
funder: U.S. DOJ, Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention (OJP)
heart: Grants of up to $750K over 36 months for states, local governments, tribes and nonprofits to run prevention, intervention and treatment for children, youth and families affected by opioid, stimulant and other SUDs, in partnership with justice and child-welfare agencies. MORE fits as clinician training (subrecipient or consultant line) inside the parent/family treatment and recovery part of an application (Objective 3). The youth-only prevention parts are a weaker fit, and MORE's evidence base is in adults.
accounts_needed: SAM.gov (UEI), Grants.gov, JustGrants for the lead applicant
page_limit: Proposal Questionnaire answers of 1-2 paragraphs each; abstract up to 2,000 characters
attachments: SF-424; Proposal Abstract; Proposal Questionnaire; Budget Detail Worksheet; Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (if applicable); Consultant Rate (if applicable); Employee compensation waiver for awards over $250K (if applicable); CVs/Resumes; Timeline; Tribal Authorizing Resolution (if applicable); Financial Management and System of Internal Controls Questionnaire; Agency Funding Priorities Inventory
scoring_map: Description of the Need 5%; Project Goals and Objectives 15%; Project Design and Implementation 35% (name subrecipients and their roles); Capabilities and Competencies 30%; Budget 15%

name: OJJDP FY 2026 Family Treatment Court Program
funder: U.S. DOJ, Office of Justice Programs, Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention (OJJDP)
program: Family Treatment Court Program (Category 1: New, Category 2: Enhancing)
heart: Four-year federal grants (Cat 1 up to $850K, Cat 2 up to $750K) for courts and local governments to start or expand family treatment courts that pay for SUD and co-occurring treatment for parents in the child welfare system, with explicit objectives for opioid and stimulant use disorders. MORE fits as evidence-based OUD/SUD treatment capacity: a county or court can budget MORE clinician training for its treatment providers as a contractor/consultant cost or through a subrecipient provider.
accounts_needed: SAM.gov (UEI), Grants.gov, JustGrants (all held by the government applicant)
match_required: Yes: 25% of total project costs (cash and/or in-kind); federal share max 75%
page_limit: No narrative page limit. Proposal Questionnaire answers of 1-2 paragraphs each, plus an abstract of up to 2,000 characters
attachments: SF-424; Proposal Questionnaire; Budget Detail Worksheet; Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (if applicable); Consultant Rate (if applicable); Employee compensation waiver (if applicable); Tribal Authorizing Resolution (if applicable); Timeline; Supplement Certification; Disclosures and assurances
scoring_map: Description of the Need 5%; Project Goals and Objectives 15%; Project Design and Implementation 35% (name subrecipients and their roles); Capabilities and Competencies 30%; Budget 15%

name: BJA FY 2026 Residential Substance Abuse Treatment (RSAT) for State Prisoners Formula Grants Program
funder: U.S. DOJ, Office of Justice Programs, Bureau of Justice Assistance
heart: Formula money to every state for SUD treatment in prisons and jails (residential, pretrial, and aftercare tracks), with a required pass-through to local jails. 'Training curricula' is a listed allowable cost, and MORE is an evidence-based treatment for OUD and co-occurring conditions that fits RSAT residential and aftercare programs as a training line item.
accounts_needed: Applicant state: SAM.gov, Grants.gov, JustGrants. More Therapy: SAM.gov/UEI helpful as a contractor or subrecipient vendor.
match_required: Yes: at least 25% of total project costs must be non-federal, cash and/or in-kind; federal share is no more than 75%
page_limit: Proposal Narrative no more than 10 pages, double-spaced, 12-pt font; abstract no more than 2,000 characters
attachments: ['Proposal Narrative', 'Budget Detail Worksheet (web form)', 'Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (if applicable)', 'Consultant Rate (if applicable)', 'Employee Compensation Limitation waiver for awards over $250,000 (if applicable)', 'Certification Regarding Non-Residential SUD Treatment-Aftercare (if applicable)']

name: Ohio AG Opioid Remediation — jail addiction programs (CY2026)
funder: Office of the Ohio Attorney General
program: Improving Outcomes for Substance-Addicted Inmates (CY2025–27, AG settlement funds)
heart: $20M/yr for county jails and CBCFs to stand up addiction programming — 'new contract services related to OUD' explicitly qualifies, so a jail grantee contracts More Therapy to train its treatment staff in MORE. Rolling review through Dec 1.
portal: Email application to JailGrants@OhioAGO.gov — rolling, quarterly payments
accounts_needed: None for More Therapy; jail needs OH|ID + OhioPays
scoring_map: AG review committee; priorities: new programming in shortage areas, multi-county sharing, multi-county jails

name: NIH/NIDA SBIR Phase I (PA-27-100)
funder: NIH / NIDA
heart: The one big pot built for for-profits — R&D money for the MORE app and training platform. Eric wants the ~$2M path; Phase I is the door. The Sep 5 date passed; the next standard due date is Jan 5, 2027.
accounts_needed: SAM/UEI (annual renewal) + SBA Company Registry + eRA Commons + Grants.gov — 6+ weeks of lead; start now
scoring_map: NIH 5-criteria review — Significance (pain+OUD unmet need), Innovation (~3× CBT effect), Approach, Investigators, Environment; NIDA caps Phase I $400K / Phase II $3M

name: Texas OAFC — criminal-justice opioid abatement (targeted cycle)
funder: TX Opioid Abatement Fund Council
program: 2026 Grant Issuance Plan (amended 3/12/2026) — Spring 2026 targeted strategy, NOFA pending
heart: Up to $25M for opioid abatement in the criminal-justice system, awards $250K–$2.5M, categories explicitly include Workforce Development and Training — train jail/reentry clinicians in MORE layered onto MOUD. NOFA overdue; watch closely.
accounts_needed: TX OGMS account
scoring_map: Plan categories: Treatment & Coordination of Care · Recovery Support · Workforce Development and Training · Prevention/Public Safety

name: NIH HEAL IMPOWR Research Centers — chronic pain + OUD (RFA-DA-28-011)
funder: NIH / NIDA (HEAL Initiative)
program: IMPOWR Health Systems, RM1 team award
heart: Health-systems implementation of integrative interventions for co-occurring chronic pain + OUD — MORE's exact dyad and evidence space, and clinician training is a core implementation strategy this NOFO funds. Team with Garland/U. Utah.
accounts_needed: SAM/UEI + eRA Commons + Grants.gov

name: NIH HEAL — Translating Addiction Research into Practice (RFA-DA-27-016)
funder: NIH / NIDA (HEAL Initiative)
heart: NIH money a for-profit can hold directly, whose stated priority is exactly MORE's pitch: getting clinicians trained in and delivering evidence-based addiction treatment, with chronic-pain-comorbid SUD named as a priority. An R61 (train clinicians, pilot fidelity) into R33 (implementation trial) built around MORE dissemination.
accounts_needed: SAM/UEI + eRA Commons (SO + PI) + Grants.gov + ORCID — 6+ weeks
page_limit: Standard NIH page limits + 2-pp Timeline and Milestone Plan attachment
scoring_map: Standard NIH peer review; R33 transition is administrative against R61 milestones. NON-RESPONSIVE traps: solely testing new interventions, purely descriptive studies — frame as translation/implementation of the established MORE evidence base.

name: NCCIH — Mind and Body Interventions via Emotional Well-Being (R61/R33, PAR-25-449)
funder: NIH / NCCIH
heart: NCCIH wants trials of mind and body practices, naming mindfulness meditation first, that work through emotional well-being. MORE's positive-affect and savoring mechanism is a direct match, and for-profits can apply.
accounts_needed: SAM/UEI, Grants.gov, eRA Commons
scoring_map: R61 milestones must justify the R33 phase; frame MORE's emotional well-being mechanism (savoring/positive affect) as the target.

name: Rural Communities Opioid Response Program - Overdose Response (FY27)
funder: HHS Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Federal Office of Rural Health Policy
heart: One-year HRSA grants of up to $300K to meet urgent overdose and SUD needs in HRSA-designated rural areas. For-profits can apply directly, and the last cycle listed clinical training (certification, CEU/CME) as an allowable activity. More Therapy could apply itself with a MORE training and implementation package for rural OUD providers, or a rural clinic or health system could apply and budget MORE training.
accounts_needed: SAM.gov UEI, Grants.gov, Login.gov; HRSA EHBs
page_limit: 40 pages in FY25 NOFO; FY27 not yet published
attachments: FY25: project abstract, project narrative, budget narrative, Attachment 1 General Project Information (used for eligibility screening), Attachment 2 target rural service area, and others. Confirm against the FY27 NOFO.

name: CCBHC Improvement & Advancement (SM-26-015)
funder: SAMHSA
program: CCBHC IA for existing clinics; CFDA 93.696; Grants.gov opp 360978
heart: The application window closed 2026-08-17. What's left is the post-award play: about 117 existing CCBHCs will each get up to $1M/yr for up to 4 years to improve services. Once SAMHSA publishes the FY26 grantees, approach the funded clinics as their EBP and workforce-training partner (budget revision or a Year-2 line).
accounts_needed: None for More Therapy; it would be a contractor line in the grantee's budget
scoring_map: A need 10-15 pts (+5 priority pts for high opioid-mortality areas); B implementation 35 pts (staffing/training live here); C EBP 5 pts (name MORE); D experience 25; E data 20
prep_needed: MORE-for-CCBHC one-pager tied to Allowable Activities #3/#10; pull the funded-org contact list once the award list publishes.
funded_list_source: SAMHSA grant awards (samhsa.gov/grants) + USASpending.gov — search CCBHC-PDI/IA FY26 grantees; check monthly from ~Nov 2026.

name: NIDA — Interventions to Prevent and Treat SUD and Overdose (UG3/UH3, PAR-25-446)
funder: NIH / NIDA
program: UG3/UH3 cooperative agreement, clinical trial optional
heart: NIDA's standing mechanism for developing and testing SUD and overdose treatments, including co-morbid SUD. It suits a MORE trial for OUD or for a stimulant or polysubstance population, and for-profits can lead.
accounts_needed: SAM/UEI, Grants.gov, eRA Commons
scoring_map: Milestone-driven UG3 to UH3 transition; needs a development-stage aim (e.g., adapting MORE for a new SUD population or delivery mode).

name: Texas OAFC — Fall 2026 CORE grants
funder: TX Opioid Abatement Fund Council
heart: Up to $75M in multi-year (3-5 yr) settlement grants across Texas's 20 RHP regions. 'Workforce Training and Development' is an eligible category, and MOUD expansion and pregnant/postpartum OUD get preference. MORE fits best as a training line-item or sub under a Texas MOUD provider in each target region. NOFA not yet posted.
accounts_needed: TX OGMS account; TX SmartBuy/CMBL ($70/yr) for vendor path

name: NIH HEAL IMPOWR BEACON Coordination Center (RFA-DA-28-012)
funder: NIH / NIDA (HEAL Initiative)
program: BEACON network coordination + capacity-building center (U2C; ALN 93.279)
heart: The single capacity-building hub for scaling evidence-based practices across the chronic pain + OUD consortium — one award, $1.75M, and clinician training at the EBP/implementation intersection is its core duty.
accounts_needed: SAM/UEI + eRA Commons + Grants.gov

name: Allegheny County OSF — annual RFP
funder: Allegheny County DHS
heart: Annual county settlement RFP — opens around November, due January. Calendar it; the county pattern of 3–6-week windows is the volume play nationwide.
accounts_needed: Bonfire vendor account (free)

name: HRSA RCORP — FY27 cycle (Overdose Response, HRSA-27-040 forecast)
funder: HRSA
heart: HRSA has forecast an FY27 RCORP-Overdose Response round (35 × $300K) that lists for-profits as eligible, which is rare for federal SUD money. MORE fits best as the evidence-based treatment/workforce piece of a rural applicant's plan (or a direct application with rural partners). Whether training is an allowable cost can't be confirmed until the NOFO posts.
accounts_needed: SAM/UEI + Grants.gov
scoring_map: FY27 known so far: Overdose Response HRSA-27-040 forecast, $10.5M total, 35 awards, $300K min = max, est. post 2027-01-11, est. due 2027-03-10, est. award 2027-08-01, start 2027-09-01. No FY27 Impact/Planning/TA forecast found in this check. FY26 shape for reference: Planning HRSA-26-036 $100K × 40 ($4M); Impact HRSA-26-037 (FY26 awards $62.7M); TA HRSA-26-038; FY26 awards also included $12.6M Overdose Response.

name: Sedgwick County / Wichita KS opioid settlement RFPs (4 programs)
funder: Sedgwick County + City of Wichita, KS
program: OUD Treatment/Recovery/Prevention RFPs 26-0080..83 (Kansas Fights Addiction Act local share)
heart: For-profits check a box on the response form and apply directly — and RFP 26-0081's Workforce Support goal ($580K, awards to $200K) explicitly funds 'continuing education and skill-building training' for behavioral-health clinicians. A straight MORE training proposal.
portal: Email submission to Purchasing@sedgwick.gov (RFP number in subject) — no portal registration
accounts_needed: None
page_limit: No hard limits; per-question word guides
scoring_map: 100 pts: understanding/methodology 25; qualifications 20; evidence-based practices 20 (MORE's RCT base); cost 15; performance measures 10; accessibility 10

name: OneOhio Recovery Foundation — Regional Grant Cycle 3 (not yet announced)
funder: OneOhio Recovery Foundation
heart: Ohio's 55% opioid-settlement foundation. Cycle 2 was $45.8M across 19 regions, and private for-profits whose services meet the Foundation's charitable purpose could apply. Workforce development / BH continuing-education priorities in some regions fit MORE training. Cycle 3 is not announced yet, and More Therapy's Ohio SoS registration under its EIN (2 consecutive years) is the gating item.
accounts_needed: Ohio SoS registration under current EIN, 2 consecutive years
scoring_map: Cycle 2 pattern: Funding Inquiry → Region review → Expert Panel → invite-only Technical Application → Grant Oversight Committee → Board approval. Applicants pick an EBP from the Evidence Guide's Pre-Approved List/Registry (Options A/B) or justify it under Option C. MORE likely goes under Option C unless listed.

name: Connecticut DMHAS — Recovery Community Centers (opioid settlement RFP)
funder: Connecticut Dept. of Mental Health and Addiction Services (Opioid Services Unit)
heart: CT is spending opioid settlement money on three low-barrier Recovery Community Centers, at $1.25M per contract over 3 years, and proprietary companies may propose. MORE fits as the evidence-based group and staff-training component inside a provider's bid.
accounts_needed: CT Secretary of State registration (partner)
scoring_map: Centers must be stigma-free, low-barrier drop-in for people who use drugs, without requiring abstinence; pitch MORE as optional skills groups plus staff training.

name: CCBHC Planning, Development & Implementation (SM-26-014)
funder: SAMHSA
program: Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics PDI
heart: The application window closed 2026-08-17 and SAMHSA's FY27 forecast has no CCBHC successor. What's left is the post-award play: about 94 new CCBHCs are expected to be funded around Nov 15, 2026, with up to $1M/yr for up to 4 years. Allowable Activity #3 (training partnerships, continuing education) lets them buy MORE training as a line item.
prep_needed: MORE-for-CCBHC one-pager tied to Allowable Activities #3/#10; pull the funded-org contact list once the award list publishes.
funded_list_source: SAMHSA grant awards (samhsa.gov/grants) + USASpending.gov — search CCBHC-PDI/IA FY26 grantees; check monthly from ~Nov 2026.

name: Improving Linkage to Care for People with Opioid Use Disorder (U01)
funder: CDC National Center for Injury Prevention and Control (NCIPC)
heart: CDC U01 research money to test strategies that overcome barriers to evidence-based OUD linkage-to-care in health care settings. MORE fits only if framed as an engagement/retention component that helps clinicians keep linked patients in care. Best led by Garland/UCSD with a health-system champion, with More Therapy as the training sub.
accounts_needed: SAM.gov UEI, Grants.gov, eRA Commons (to confirm in NOFO)

name: Rural Communities Opioid Response Program - Community Systems Development (FY2027)
funder: HRSA Federal Office of Rural Health Policy
heart: New RCORP line that pays for formalized rural networks to expand regional behavioral-health systems of care through coordinated, evidence-based SUD prevention, treatment and recovery services. MORE is an evidence-based SUD/OUD treatment with chronic-pain overlap that network clinicians can be trained in. The most realistic role is training vendor for a rural network applicant, since only 6 awards are expected and the program is built around networks.
accounts_needed: SAM.gov UEI, Grants.gov, HRSA EHBs (standard HRSA)

name: Maryland Opioid Restitution Fund Grant Program (MOOR NOFA) — next cycle TBD
funder: Maryland Office of Overdose Response
program: ORF Grant Program (settlement Exhibit E uses); 2027 cycle closed, next round not announced
heart: Maryland settlement money, up to $1M per 2-year project, for evidence-based treatment and staff training. MORE can be a named training/subcontract line in a nonprofit partner's application. The 2027 round closed; watch the award list for funded partners and for the next NOFA.
accounts_needed: Partner needs 501(c) letter, MD SDAT good standing, charity registration, 990, W-9; no SAM/Grants.gov
scoring_map: Staff eligibility screen → Evaluation Committee ranking. 2027 NOFA §5.3 criteria include quality/feasibility of timeline; budget judged on alignment with applicant funding limit and detailed justification. Must align with settlement Exhibit E provision.

name: Ohio SOS 4.0 (SOR pass-through) — Year 3 RFA watch
funder: Ohio Dept. of Behavioral Health (DBH, ex-OhioMHAS)
program: SAMHSA State Opioid Response pass-through (award H79TI087745, ~$101M/yr)
heart: Ohio's ~$100M/yr SOR pass-through explicitly funds 'expanding evidence-based practices' and names for-profit licensed community BH providers as eligible applicants — MORE training fits as the EBP line item in provider and ADAMH board applications when Year-3 RFAs post (~fall).
accounts_needed: None for More Therapy (partner applies)
scoring_map: RFA #109 awards ran $100K–$6M per applicant; short spend windows — partners need MORE priced and ready before RFAs drop

name: CA HCAI BHSA WET Plan — workforce training vendor watch
funder: California HCAI
program: Behavioral Health Services Act (Prop 1) Workforce Education & Training Plan 2026–2030, Objective 1
heart: HCAI will fund development and statewide delivery of training modules cross-training MH and SUD providers in substance-use treatment, MAT, and harm reduction for LCSW/LMFT/LPCC/psychologists — a near-exact description of MORE clinician training, with CEU alignment planned. No RFP yet; implementation began 7/1/2026.
accounts_needed: Cal eProcure vendor registration (free) when the time comes
scoring_map: Objective 1 sequence: core competencies → skills-gap analysis → map existing programs → fund module development → delivery to county agencies

name: DoD CDMRP — chronic pain research (PRMRP / CPMRP)
funder: US Dept. of Defense — CDMRP
program: Peer Reviewed Medical Research Program + Chronic Pain Management Research Program
heart: Rare for-profit-direct DoD money for chronic-pain research — MORE's pain dyad fits squarely. FY26 entry is closed; FY27 opens ~spring 2027, so we prep and apply on day one.
accounts_needed: SAM/UEI + Grants.gov + eBRAP
scoring_map: Peer + programmatic review; frame MORE as a non-pharmacological chronic-pain intervention with military/veteran relevance

name: NIH Dissemination & Implementation Research in Health (R01, PAR-25-144)
funder: NIH (multi-institute, incl. NIDA/NCCIH)
program: R01, clinical trial optional (R21 companion PAR-25-143)
heart: Funds research on how evidence-based treatments get adopted and scaled. That is exactly the question of clinician training and implementation for MORE in health systems, so the study's implementation strategy can be MORE training itself.
accounts_needed: SAM/UEI, Grants.gov, eRA Commons
scoring_map: Implementation-science framing (strategy, outcomes, framework); MORE as the EBP, training/facilitation as the strategy under test.

name: Pilot and Feasibility Studies in Preparation for Substance Use and HIV Prevention Intervention and Services Research Trials (R34 Clinical Trial Optional)
funder: National Institutes of Health / NIDA (OAR, ODP co-fund)
program: NIDA DESPR R34 pilot & feasibility PAR
heart: Three-year R34 grants (up to $450k direct costs in total) for pilot and feasibility work ahead of effectiveness or implementation trials in SUD treatment and recovery services. Pain-co-occurring populations and addiction-workforce training are named priorities. MORE fits as a pilot of a MORE implementation or training strategy (e.g., fidelity and workforce capacity in a new setting such as an OTP, FQHC or treatment court) or an adaptation for an understudied population. Dr. Garland/UCSD would be the likely applicant, with More Therapy as the training subcontractor; More Therapy is also eligible to apply directly.
accounts_needed: SAM.gov UEI, Grants.gov, eRA Commons (organization + PD/PI)
page_limit: Per NIH Table of Page Limits (R34 Research Strategy is typically 12 pp; confirm in table)
attachments: Standard NIH R application forms incl. Human Subjects/Clinical Trial info (clinical trial optional)
scoring_map: Standard NIH peer review criteria for R34 (significance, investigators, innovation, approach, environment), per NOFO Section V

name: Emergency Department Alternatives to Opioids Program (ED-ALT) FY2027
funder: SAMHSA / Center for Substance Abuse Treatment
heart: Hospital and ED grants to replace opioids in ED pain care with alternatives, including required staff training and non-drug psychosocial pain treatment followed by referral to ongoing care. MORE fits as the evidence-based psychosocial pain/OUD treatment patients are referred to after the ED visit, and as the staff-training vendor for a hospital applicant.
accounts_needed: Hospital applicant: SAM.gov UEI, Grants.gov, eRA Commons
attachments: FY26: Letters of Commitment (Attachment 1), data instruments, consent forms, timeline (2 pp), bios (2 pp), SPOC letter, nonprofit documentation, indirect rate

name: City of Richmond Opioid Settlement Funds RFA (next cycle)
funder: City of Richmond, VA - Office of Opioid and Substance Use Response
program: Opioid Settlement Funds Request for Applications
heart: Richmond grants opioid settlement money to nonprofits and local government entities for evidence-based prevention, treatment and recovery. A 2026 priority was adding evidence-based treatments across treatment settings, so MORE training fits as a line-item in a provider's project.
attachments: Cover sheet (Attachment A); Microsoft Form application; Proof of liability insurance; Federal tax-exempt certification; Most recent full IRS Form 990; Project budget; Budget narrative; Timeline; Current-year operating budget
scoring_map: Community Impact and Lived Experience 25; Program Design and Evidence Based Practices 25; Connection Across Continuum of Care 20 (+10 bonus for joint applications); Data Collection and Outside Reporting 15; Cost-Effectiveness and Budget 15

name: AHCCCS State Opioid Response IV (SOR IV) subawards
funder: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS) / SAMHSA
heart: Arizona's SOR IV federal funds pay for OUD treatment, integrated care and recovery services across AHCCCS's provider network through 2027-09-29. Training providers in MORE, an evidence-based OUD and chronic-pain intervention, fits the program goal of expanding access to OUD treatment.

name: Springfield Opioid Recovery and Remediation Fund (ORRF) Mini-Grant Program, next cycle (2026-2027)
funder: City of Springfield, MA – Health and Human Services
heart: Springfield's yearly opioid settlement mini-grants. If MORE clinician training is an allowable cost, a local treatment or recovery provider could include it in its budget.

name: Tennessee Opioid Abatement Council Community Grants – Cycle 4
funder: Tennessee Opioid Abatement Council (administered with TDMHSAS)
program: OAC Community Grants (65% share of TN Opioid Abatement Fund)
heart: Three-year statewide opioid settlement grants to Tennessee-based agencies for prevention, harm reduction, treatment, recovery support, education/training and research. 40% is set aside for treatment and 10% for education/training, so a TN treatment provider can put MORE clinician training in its budget.
portal: Sub-Recipient Grant Management Enterprise Solution, State of Tennessee (the portal used for Cycle 3)
accounts_needed: State of Tennessee sub-recipient grant portal account (applicant partner)

name: Rural Communities Opioid Response Program - Child and Adolescent Behavioral Health (RCORP-CABH) FY2027
funder: HRSA Federal Office of Rural Health Policy
heart: About 9 four-year consortium grants, up to $1M each, to set up and expand behavioral health services (MH and SUD) for rural youth aged 5-17. MORE could fit only as a training vendor to a rural consortium if the NOFO allows workforce training and adolescent SUD treatment; MORE's evidence base is adult, so the fit is weak.
accounts_needed: SAM.gov UEI, Grants.gov, HRSA EHBs (for applicant)

name: Arizona State share of opioid settlement funds (One Arizona Agreement)
funder: Arizona Attorney General's Office / Arizona Legislature
heart: The State's opioid settlement share is appropriated to state agencies for approved purposes, including OUD treatment and prison/jail SUD programs. MORE training could enter as a line item in an agency program, e.g. ADCRR's SUD treatment program.
